648:     /// Run VUNUS check: variable assigned in all branches but unused after.
649:     fn check_vunus(
650:         &self,
651:         table: &SymbolTable,
652:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
653:     ) {
654:         if self.is_check_disabled("VUNUS") {
655:             return;
656:         }
657: 
658:         for scope in &table.scopes {
659:             let output_args: HashSet<&str> = scope
660:                 .defs
661:                 .iter()
662:                 .filter(|d| d.kind == DefKind::OutputArg)
663:                 .map(|d| d.name.as_str())
664:                 .collect();
665: 
666:             // Find variables with multiple defs but no uses.
667:             let mut def_counts: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
668:             for def in &scope.defs {
669:                 if def.kind == DefKind::Assignment {
670:                     *def_counts.entry(def.name.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
671:                 }
672:             }
673: 
674:             for (name, count) in &def_counts {
675:                 if *count < 2 {
676:                     continue;
677:                 }
678:                 if output_args.contains(name) {
679:                     continue;
680:                 }
681:                 if self.should_ignore_name(name) {
682:                     continue;
683:                 }
684:                 if !scope.is_used(name) {
685:                     // Find the last definition for this variable.
686:                     if let Some(last_def) = scope
687:                         .defs
688:                         .iter()
689:                         .rev()
690:                         .find(|d| d.name == *name && d.kind == DefKind::Assignment)
691:                     {
692:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
693:                             rule_id: "VUNUS",
694:                             message: format!(
695:                                 "Variable '{name}' is assigned in multiple branches but never used after"
696:                             ),
697:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
698:                             byte_range: last_def.byte_range.clone(),
699:                             line: last_def.line,
700:                             column: last_def.column,
701:                             fix: None,
702:                         });
703:                     }
704:                 }
705:             }
706:         }
707:     }

711:     fn check_msnu(
712:         &self,
713:         ctx: &FileContext,
714:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
715:     ) {
716:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNU") {

718:         }

720:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
721:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();

723:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
724:             ctx.tree.root_node(),

726:             &mut field_writes,

731:         for write in &field_writes {

734:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
735:                     rule_id: "MSNU",
736:                     message: format!(
737:                         "Struct field '{}.{}' is set but never read",
738:                         write.object, write.field
739:                     ),
740:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
741:                     byte_range: write.byte_range.clone(),
742:                     line: write.line,

750:     /// Run MSNE check: struct field doesn't exist (assigned but potential typo).
751:     /// Heuristic: if a struct has many fields and one is only written once with
752:     /// no reads, it may be a typo.
753:     fn check_msne(
754:         &self,
755:         ctx: &FileContext,
756:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
757:     ) {
758:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNE") {
759:             return;
760:         }
761: 
762:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
763:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
764: 
765:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
766:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
767:             ctx.source,
768:             &mut field_writes,
769:             &mut field_reads,
770:         );
771: 
772:         // Group writes by object name.
773:         let mut writes_by_object: HashMap<&str, Vec<&FieldAccess>> = HashMap::new();
774:         for write in &field_writes {
775:             writes_by_object
776:                 .entry(write.object.as_str())
777:                 .or_default()
778:                 .push(write);
779:         }
780: 
781:         // For each object with multiple fields written, check if any field
782:         // is written exactly once and never read — potential typo.
783:         for (object, writes) in &writes_by_object {
784:             if writes.len() < 2 {
785:                 continue;
786:             }
787: 
788:             let mut field_write_count: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
789:             for w in writes {
790:                 *field_write_count.entry(w.field.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
791:             }
792: 
793:             for w in writes {
794:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", object, w.field);
795:                 if field_write_count.get(w.field.as_str()) == Some(&1) && !field_reads.contains(&key)
796:                 {
797:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
798:                         rule_id: "MSNE",
799:                         message: format!(
800:                             "Struct field '{}.{}' is assigned once and never read (possible typo)",
801:                             object, w.field
802:                         ),
803:                         severity: Severity::Info,
804:                         byte_range: w.byte_range.clone(),
805:                         line: w.line,
806:                         column: w.column,
807:                         fix: None,
808:                     });
809:                 }
810:             }
811:         }
812:     }

814:     /// Collect field accesses (both reads and writes) from the parse tree.
815:     fn collect_field_accesses(
816:         node: Node,
817:         source: &str,
818:         writes: &mut Vec<FieldAccess>,
819:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
820:     ) {
821:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
822:             // Check if LHS is a field_expression.
823:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
824:                 if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
825:                     if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(lhs, source) {
826:                         writes.push(access);
827:                     }
828:                 }
829:             }
830:             // Check RHS for field reads.
831:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
832:                 Self::collect_field_reads(rhs, source, reads);
833:             }
834:         } else if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
835:             // A field_expression not on the LHS of assignment is a read.
836:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
837:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
838:                 reads.insert(key);
839:             }
840:         }
841: 
842:         // Recurse into children (skip assignment children we already handled).
843:         if node.kind() != "assignment" {
844:             let count = node.child_count();
845:             for i in 0..count {
846:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
847:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
848:                 }
849:             }
850:         } else {
851:             // For assignments, recurse into children except LHS field_expression.
852:             let count = node.child_count();
853:             for i in 0..count {
854:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
855:                     if child.kind() == "field_expression" {
856:                         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
857:                             if lhs.id() == child.id() {
858:                                 continue;
859:                             }
860:                         }
861:                     }
862:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
863:                 }
864:             }
865:         }
866:     }
867: 
868:     /// Collect field reads from an expression subtree.
869:     fn collect_field_reads(
870:         node: Node,
871:         source: &str,
872:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
873:     ) {
874:         if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
875:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
876:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
877:                 reads.insert(key);
878:             }
879:         }
880: 
881:         let count = node.child_count();
882:         for i in 0..count {
883:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
884:                 Self::collect_field_reads(child, source, reads);
885:             }
886:         }
887:     }
888: }

948: /// Recursively walk tree to find statement-level expressions with no effect.
949: fn walk_for_no_effect(
950:     node: Node,
951:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
952:     noeff_disabled: bool,
953:     eqeff_disabled: bool,
954: ) {
955:     // Check if this node is at statement level (parent is block or source_file).
956:     let is_statement_level = node
957:         .parent()
958:         .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
959:         .unwrap_or(false);
960: 
961:     if is_statement_level {
962:         let kind = node.kind();
963: 
964:         // EQEFF: comparison operator at statement level.
965:         if !eqeff_disabled && kind == COMPARISON_NODE {
966:             let pos = node.start_position();
967:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
968:                 rule_id: "EQEFF",
969:                 message: "Comparison has no effect (result is not used)".to_string(),
970:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
971:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
972:                 line: pos.row + 1,
973:                 column: pos.column + 1,
974:                 fix: None,
975:             });
976:         }
977:         // NOEFF: other expression nodes at statement level that are not
978:         // assignments, function_calls, or commands.
979:         else if !noeff_disabled && NO_EFFECT_EXPR_NODES.contains(&kind) {
980:             let pos = node.start_position();
981:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
982:                 rule_id: "NOEFF",
983:                 message: "Statement has no effect (expression result is discarded)"
984:                     .to_string(),
985:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
986:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
987:                 line: pos.row + 1,
988:                 column: pos.column + 1,
989:                 fix: None,
990:             });
991:         }
992:     }
993: 
994:     // Recurse into children.
995:     let count = node.child_count();
996:     for i in 0..count {
997:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
998:             walk_for_no_effect(child, diagnostics, noeff_disabled, eqeff_disabled);
999:         }
1000:     }
1001: }

1022: /// Extract a `FieldAccess` from a `field_expression` node.
1023: fn extract_field_access(node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<FieldAccess> {
1024:     // field_expression has an object and a field child.
1025:     let object_node = node.child(0)?;
1026:     let field_node = node.child_by_field_name("field")?;
1027: 
1028:     // Only handle simple identifier objects (not chained field access).
1029:     if object_node.kind() != "identifier" {
1030:         return None;
1031:     }
1032: 
1033:     let object = source[object_node.start_byte()..object_node.end_byte()].to_string();
1034:     let field = source[field_node.start_byte()..field_node.end_byte()].to_string();
1035:     let pos = node.start_position();
1036: 
1037:     Some(FieldAccess {
1038:         object,
1039:         field,
1040:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1041:         line: pos.row + 1,
1042:         column: pos.column + 1,
1043:     })
1044: }

1046: /// Simple glob pattern matching supporting `*` (any sequence) and `?` (single char).
1047: fn matches_simple_glob(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
1048:     let pat: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();
1049:     let txt: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
1050:     glob_match_recursive(&pat, &txt, 0, 0)
1051: }
1052: 
1053: /// Recursive glob matching helper.
1054: fn glob_match_recursive(pat: &[char], txt: &[char], pi: usize, ti: usize) -> bool {
1055:     if pi == pat.len() {
1056:         return ti == txt.len();
1057:     }
1058: 
1059:     match pat[pi] {
1060:         '*' => {
1061:             // `*` matches zero or more characters.
1062:             for i in ti..=txt.len() {
1063:                 if glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, i) {
1064:                     return true;
1065:                 }
1066:             }
1067:             false
1068:         }
1069:         '?' => {
1070:             // `?` matches exactly one character.
1071:             if ti < txt.len() {
1072:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
1073:             } else {
1074:                 false
1075:             }
1076:         }
1077:         c => {
1078:             if ti < txt.len() && txt[ti] == c {
1079:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
1080:             } else {
1081:                 false
1082:             }
1083:         }
1084:     }
1085: }

def line_end(match):

def find_line_start(pos):

def match_braces(pos):

    Assumes braces in the source are balanced."""
    i = text.index("{", pos)
    depth = 0
    while i < len(text):
        c = text[i]

        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1

def extract_anchored(marker_regex):
    """Extract a doc-commented item whose definition line matches `marker_regex`.

    closing brace of the first '{' in the definition line. Returns
    (block_text, end_offset).

    m = re.search(marker_regex, text, re.M)
    if not m:

    start = find_line_start(m.start())

        prev_line = text[prev_start:prev_end]

    end = match_braces(m.start())

    tests_with_comments = module_tests(module)
    files[module] = build_check_file(module, CHECK_DOCS[module], methods,

    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

    print(f"wrote {path} ({len(content.splitlines())} lines)")

def find_block(src, start_marker):
    """Extract doc-commented fn/test block: walk back over /// lines from
    start_marker, then brace-match forward. Returns (block, ok)."""
    m = re.search(start_marker, src, re.M)
    if not m:
        return None, False
    start = src.rfind("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
    while start > 0:
        prev_end = start - 1
        prev_start = src.rfind("\n", 0, prev_end) + 1
        if re.match(r"^\s*///", src[prev_start:prev_end]):

    depth = 0
    while i < len(src):
        c = src[i]
        if c == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return src[start:i + 1], True
        i += 1
    return None, False
